messages:
sanjay: heads-up — after the deploy I'm seeing a bad interaction between eviction and prefix pinning when shards are shared across tenants. some requests get served stale prefixes, others get OOM-ish spikes. wondering if we should pick a stronger serialization model for eviction ops.
marina: can you paste the log snippet?
sanjay: sure, here's the tail: ```
2026-03-19T14:02:10Z shard-7 evict prefix tenantA/pfx_123 start lease=none
2026-03-19T14:02:10Z shard-7 pin prefix tenantB/pfx_123 count=1
2026-03-19T14:02:10Z shard-7 evict prefix tenantA/pfx_123 completed (partial)
2026-03-19T14:02:10Z shard-7 pin prefix tenantA/pfx_123 reloaded from origin
```
marina: looks like concurrent evict + pin; pin logic doesn't wait for a coherent view. :confused:
lucy: two obvious approaches: lease-based ownership per-shard (fast, local) or centralized sequencer per-shard (strong ordering).
deva: leases are attractive for perf but expiry semantics bite. if a lease expires and another actor evicts, we can get double-evict/race where a pin thinks data is still valid. we had similar bug with KV index rebuilds. tombstones + version tags could help.
ton y: central sequencer simplifies correctness: make every eviction a sequenced op, pins consult sequencer position. downside is added RTT for the fast path. sequencer could be colocated though.
sanjay: what about hybrid: local lease for fast path, but if we detect cross-tenant prefix name collisions or >X concurrent ops, escalate to sequencer?
lucy: yes — heuristics: if prefix namespace is exclusive to tenant, local lease is fine. if namespace is shared (e.g., index-derived prefixes) go to sequencer. also add a small tombstone window to prevent immediate re-materialization.
deva: tombstones need retention bounds and compaction. propose tombstone metadata: {prefix, version, evict_ts, owner_lease_id}. pins compare version before using cache.
marina: can we do a cheap check: pin fetch does an atomic read of prefix meta (version + evict_ts). if evict_ts > pin_start return MISS and retry. no global coordination required for common case.
ton y: that still leaves reordering where pin reads before evict_ts write. sequencer prevents that. but maybe accept eventual correctness if we bound retry attempts.
ops-bot: alert: shard-7 evict-rate spike 14:02:10 - 14:05:00 (sustained)
sanjay: ops-bot noted the spike. operationally want to avoid tail-latency regressions. any microbench estimates for sequencer latency?
lucy: local lease median path adds ~200us. sequencer add ~1.5ms median if colocated with shard leader, 5-10ms if cross-datacenter.
deva: tradeoff table: local lease = low latency, tricky correctness corners; sequencer = simple correctness, higher p99. tombstones + versioning = middle ground, requires metadata write on evict and slightly more storage.
marina: implementation plan suggestion: 1) prototype lease+tombstone on a single shard type; 2) add pin atomic meta-check (version+evict_ts); 3) run canary with shared-namespace workloads; 4) if instability persists, implement sequencer escalation path.
sanjay: +1. also add integration tests that simulate lease flaps and delayed writes (injectable network delays).
ton y: add metrics: prefix_eviction_version_conflicts, prefix_pin_retries, prefix_tombstone_compactions. those will prove model.
marina: quick config sketch: ```yaml
kv_cache:
  eviction:
    mode: hybrid
    lease_ttl_ms: 250
    tombstone_window_ms: 5000
    sequencer_threshold_concurrent_ops: 8
```
deva: test matrix: lease_ttl {50,250,1000}, tombstone_window {1s,5s,30s}, sequencer_threshold {1,8,64}. run with synthetic skewed prefixes.
sanjay: ok owners: lucy spikes the prototype code, marina wires metrics and canary harness, deva writes integration tests and failure injection, tony enumerates ops rollback plan. i'll post a short ADR draft this week.
marina: sounds good. can we also include a simple user-facing doc snippet so Dedicated customers understand hybrid guarantees?
ton y: yes, we should be explicit: "hybrid model provides best-effort immediate availability, with strong ordering fallback for conflicting namespaces".
sanjay: thanks all. i'll create the PR for the prototype branch and link here. :rocket:
